references.text: Moses reminds the Israelites that they were slaves in Egypt and that the Lord brought them out with a strong hand. This is the basis for keeping the Sabbath and showing mercy to others.
Israel's slavery in Egypt is used as a reason to free Hebrew servants after six years of service, following the same pattern of remembering slavery as motivation for compassion.
The reminder of slavery in Egypt is given as a reason to keep the Feast of Weeks and include the poor and foreigners in the celebration.
The same chapter contains a similar reminder of slavery in Egypt as a basis for treating immigrants, orphans, and widows with justice.
The Israelites must not oppress or harass immigrants because they themselves were immigrants in Egypt. This is the same principle of remembering the past as a foundation for ethical action.
A reminder that the Israelites know the soul of an immigrant because they themselves were immigrants in Egypt, serving as a basis for treating foreigners well.
The command to love the immigrant as oneself, based on the fact that the Israelites were immigrants in Egypt.
